attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select a preset color palette to customize the project image and tile assets with?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ What color shades might be useful for the 4 background image assets, 4 road tile assets, and 4 sprite image assets that will be used in this project?

❓What do you notice about the different preset color palette options?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the Ninja that they will be customize 4 background image assets, 4 road tile assets, and 4 sprite image assets in this project, so they should make sure that the color palette they select includes a range of colors.

💡Prompt the Ninja to notice that each of the preset color palettes still only has 16 possible colors. Each palette varies in terms of shade brightness and RGB values selected. They should consider the “vibe” of their project - would it be helpful to use colors with a strong contrast, or softer tones?
steps.instructions:
Start the project by customizing the Assets menu color palette!


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen. On the left side menu, click on the Colors button. 


Notice that the color palette is set to the default Arcade theme. Click the Arcade dropdown menu to view the different preset color palette options.


In this project, 4 background image assets, 4 road tile assets, and 4 sprite image assets will be customized. Think about what colors might be useful for this project, then select a related preset color palette and click Apply.

steps.hints: ❓Did you pick an image from the Gallery that has many solid colors that are easy to fill and modify?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which image from the Gallery might you use as a template for the 4 background image assets?

❓ How might you use the different tools in the paint editor to create 4 unique background image assets?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to include an index number when naming each background image asset (starting from 0, 1, 2, 3).

💡 As the ninja is selecting a background image from the Gallery, point out that it might be useful to pick an image that has many solid colors that are easy to fill and modify. 

💡 After the ninja has selected their background image, have them consider which colors will be easiest to change in the image, as well as what colors they might replace them with to create a unique scene.
steps.instructions:
Customize a background image to create 4 unique assets to start the project!


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen. Create a new image asset, then select a background image from the Gallery. Rename the asset backgroundImage0.


Duplicate the background image asset 3 times, so that there are 4 background image assets total. In each new asset, use the fill tool to change the colors of the image, the marquee tool to rearrange elements in the image, or the paint tool to add to the existing scene. 


Customize each asset so that each one uses the same background image in a unique way. Rename the background image assets: backgroundImage1, backgroundImage2, and backgroundImage3.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the same number in each tile asset’s name as the background image that it matches with?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which tile image from the Gallery might you use as a template for the 4 tile assets?

❓ How might you use the different tools in the paint editor to match each tile with a specific background image?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to make sure they’ve named the tile assets using the same index number as its matching background image asset.

💡 After the ninja has selected their tile image, have them consider which colors will be easiest to change, as well as what colors they should replace them with to create a unique scene.

💡 Prompt the ninja to match each new tile asset with a previously created background image. Have them consider what unique characteristics each tile might have to differentiate each scene.
steps.instructions:
Customize a tile to create 4 unique tile assets to match each background image!


Create a new tile asset, then select a tile from the Gallery that matches the backgroundImage0 asset. Give the asset a descriptive name, followed by the number 0.


Duplicate the tile asset 3 times, so that there are 4 tile assets total. In each new asset, use the fill tool to change the colors of the tile, the marquee tool to resize or rearrange elements in the tile, or the paint tool to add onto the existing tile. 


Customize each asset so that each one can be matched to one of the background image assets. Rename the tile assets with the same number as the background image asset that they match with.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you resize the image canvas to 24 x 24 pixels, then use the marquee tool to resize the sprite image to fill the canvas?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How can you change the dimensions of an image canvas in the paint editor?

❓ How might you use the different tools in the paint editor to create a unique persona for each Player sprite, that matches a background image and tile asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to make sure they’ve named the sprite image assets using the same index number as its matching tile and background image assets.

💡 As the ninja is creating their unique sprite image assets, have them look through the existing matching background image and tile assets to consider what type of persona might pair well with each scene.

💡 As the ninja is tinkering, encourage them to rearrange, erase, and draw new elements in each sprite image. Prompt them to continue tinkering with different colors until they come up with 4 unique sprite image assets.
steps.instructions:
Customize a sprite image to create 4 unique sprite image assets to match each scene!


Create a new image asset, and set the canvas size to 24 x 24 pixels. Then select a character image from the Gallery that matches the backgroundImage0 and tile0 assets, and use the marquee tool to resize the sprite’s dimensions to fill the canvas. Give the asset a descriptive name, followed by the number 0.


Duplicate the sprite image asset 3 times, so that there are 4 sprite image assets total. In each new asset, use the fill tool to change the colors of the image, the erase tool to remove elements in the image, or the paint tool to add on to the existing sprite image. 


Consider what unique personas each sprite might take on and what elements can be added or taken away, to differentiate their appearances. Rename the sprite image assets with the same number as the background image and tile assets that they match with.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the tile0 asset from My Tiles to design a tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ Which asset should be used to create a path of tiles on a tilemap asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to make sure that they’ve used the tile0 asset from My Tiles to design their tilemap asset. This will make sure that all subsequent tile assets added to the screen match their corresponding background and sprite image assets.
steps.instructions:
Create a tilemap to display tiles on the bottom of the screen.


Create a new tilemap asset and change the dimensions of the canvas to 10 x 8, so that the tilemap is the size of the screen.


Using the tile0 asset from My Tiles, create a line of tiles from left to right along the bottom of the screen. Give the tilemap asset a descriptive name.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type assets, a dot operator, the asset type and the asset name inside 2 backticks `` for each element in the 3 arrays?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ Does each matching background image, tile, and sprite image have the same index number in each array?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation if they need assistance declaring an array and adding image and tile assets as its elements.

💡 Prompt the ninja to make sure that each array lists its elements in order of index number, so that the corresponding background image, tile, and sprite image all have the same index.
steps.instructions:
Store the customized assets in arrays!


Return to the JavaScript editor, then start the project with a // game initialization comment. 


Below, create spriteImages, roadTiles, and backgroundImages arrays to store each of the customized assets. Inside the brackets of each array, type the names of the corresponding image and tile assets from My Assets, separated by commas. 


Be sure to match each element’s index with the number in its asset name. Each matching background image, tile, and sprite image asset should have the same index number.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you place the currentIndex inside the brackets of the backgroundImages array in the setBackgroundImage parameter?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ How might the currentIndex variable be used in this project?

❓ Which background image is displayed when the project starts?

❓ What function should be used to display a tilemap on screen?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the project starts, the background image at index 0 of the backgroundImages array and the tilemap asset will be displayed on screen.

💡 The currentIndex variable will be used to keep track of which index number is currently being used to display assets on the screen. This will be updated later in the project to cycle through each of the matching sets of customized assets.

💡 Remind the ninja to check the documentation if they need help displaying a tilemap on screen.
steps.instructions:
Display the first background image on screen!


Declare a currentIndex variable set to 0. 


Below this, add a // game start comment, then display the background image set to the currentIndex of the backgroundImages array.


Underneath, add code to display the tilemap asset underneath the setBackgroundImage function. 


Click ▶ to see the first element in the backgroundImages array and the tilemap asset displayed on screen!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you place the currentIndex inside the brackets of the spriteImages array in the sprites.create image parameter?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What should the Player sprite’s image parameter be set to?

❓ Where might the Player sprite be placed on the screen, so that it is in the middle of the tilemap design?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use documentation for assistance adding a sprite and placing it on the tilemap.

💡 The currentIndex of the spriteImages array should be used as the Player sprite’s image argument so that the image can easily be updated throughout the project.
steps.instructions:
Add a Player sprite to the project!


Under // game start, add a Player sprite with its image set to the currentIndex of the spriteImages array.


Place the Player sprite on the tilemap, in the middle of the screen.


Click ▶ to test out the Player sprite’s code.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the newIndex parameter in the setImage and setBackgroundImage function parameters?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓What words and symbols should be used to add a number parameter to a function definition?

❓What will happen when the changeScene function is called?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation for assistance adding a parameter to a function definition.

💡 When the changeScene function is called, the Player sprite’s image will be set to the index passed to the function of the spriteImages array and the background image will be set to the index passed to the function of the backgroundImages array.
steps.instructions:
Create a function to change the project’s scene!


Define a changeScene function with a newIndex number parameter that will be used to set the new index in each array.


Inside the function definition, set the Player sprite’s image to the newIndex of the spriteImages array.


Underneath, set the background image to the newIndex of the backgroundImages array.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the getTilesByType function to make something happen to every element in the array of currentTile assets?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What value is stored in the currentTile variable?

❓ What function retrieves all tiles of a specific type? Why might that be useful?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The currentTile variable will store the tile image currently displayed on screen and will be used in the for element of loop to make something to happen to every tile on screen.
steps.instructions:
Change the tilemap tiles when the scene changes!


Declare a currentTile variable under // game initialization set to the currentIndex of the roadTiles array.


In the changeScene function definition, set up a for element of loop that will make something happen to every tile that is one of the currentTile assets.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the loop’s element variable, a dot operator, and the column and row properties to set the location of the new tiles?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen to the array of currentTile images when the changeScene function is called?

❓ Why should the currentTile variable be reassigned after the for element of loop runs in the changeScene function definition?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the changeScene function is called, the array of currentTile images will be replaced with the tile image at the new index value of the tiles array.

💡 The currentTile variable needs to be reassigned after the for element of loop runs in the changeScene function so that the next time the function is called, the currentTile variable stores the tile that is displayed on the screen.
steps.instructions:
Set a new tile at the location of the existing tiles on the tilemap!


Inside the for element of loop inside the changeScene function definition, set a new tile at each element’s column and row tilemap coordinates. Set the new tile’s image to the newIndex of the tiles array.


Below the for element of loop, set the currentTile variable to the newIndex of the tiles array, to update the tile used the next time the function is called.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use an increment operator ++ to increase the value of currentIndex by 1?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the B button is pressed?

❓ What symbols should be used to check the value of the currentIndex variable, assign it a new value, and to increase its value by 1?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the B button is pressed, the project will check to see if the currentIndex variable is equal to 3, so that it cycles back to the beginning of the image assets. If it is not equal to 3, the variable will be increased by 1. After, the changeScene function is called, passing the new value of the currentIndex variable as the parameter.

💡 Remind the ninja that an equality operator == should be used to check the value of a variable, an assignment operator = should be used to assign a new value to the variable, and an increment operator ++ can be used to increase the value of the variable by 1.
steps.instructions:
Change the value of the currentIndex variable when the B button is pressed!


Add a // game events comment then add an event that will run when the B button is pressed. Use a conditional to first check if the currentIndex variable is 3. If so, reassign the variable a value of 0. Else, increase the value of the variable by 1. 


Below the conditional, call the changeScene function, passing the currentIndex variable as the parameter.


Click ▶ to test the image changes when the B button is pressed.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the setDialogTextColor to change the font color of the instructions?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What function and color might be used to change the text color in the dialog box?

❓ What images might be used for the dialog frame and cursor?


Sensei Pro Tip:


💡 Encourage the ninja to use the marquee tool in the editor to resize the cursor image.
steps.instructions:
Add instructions to the beginning of the project!


Under // game start, set the dialog frame and dialog text color below the code that sets the background image and tilemap. 


Then, create a dialog box to share instructions for the project with the user.


Click ▶ to play the completed project!

subgroups.title: A Change of Scenery
subgroups.introduction: Customize an existing sprite image, background image, and tile assets to create a project with 4 unique scenes!

validationItems.text: Use an alternative preset color palette in the Assets menu.
Customize 4 background image assets, 4 tile assets, and 4 sprite image assets. Store the assets in backgroundImages, roadTiles, and spriteImages arrays.
Declare a currentIndex variable and use it to set the background image and Player sprite image from each array.
Display a tilemap asset on screen.
Define a changeScene function with a newIndex number parameter to change the Player sprite’s image and the background image.
Use a for element of loop and the function’s number parameter to update each tile’s image. Use a currentTile variable to store the tile image.
Call the changeScene function when the B button is pressed. Update the currentIndex variable so it continually cycles through each asset in the arrays.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about pixel art and how to use the asset editor to modify an existing asset. You will also use code from the Scroller and Images categories to enrich the project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Remixologist
badges.description: Use the paint editor to modify and remix existing pixel art image assets.

badges.title: Doppelganger
badges.description: Edit an existing asset to create multiple versions of the same image.

badges.title: Nice Change of Scenery
badges.description: Use the Scroller extension to create a background that scrolls and changes images as a sprite “walks”.

badges.title: Swatch and Learn
badges.description: Write code to get, set, and replace a pixel’s color on an image asset.

badges.title: A Refined Palette
badges.description: Use RGB values or hex color code to change the colors of the code editor’s color palette.

badges.title: Mixing it Up
badges.description: Use the Color Palette tool to change the default color palette with different colors.
